value.emollient_frequency: as normally used by the subjects, applied to non-treated areas only, not within 12 hours of a study visit
prohibited_concomitant: All other biologics -- 12-week washout before Day 0
Oral corticosteroids, retinoids, apremilast, roflumilast, methotrexate, cyclosporine, fumarates, and other systemic immunosuppressants -- 4-week washout before Day 0
Medicated shampoos (eg, coal tar, keratolytics, antifungals, zinc pyrithione, selenium sulfide, corticosteroids, medical devices) -- 2-week washout before Day 0, and prohibited during the study
Topical medications used on the scalp for conditions besides psoriasis (eg, topical minoxidil for androgenetic alopecia) -- 4-week washout before Day 0
Topical anti-psoriasis medications (eg, topical corticosteroids, vitamin D analogs, prescription shampoos), except emollients -- 2-week washout before Day 0
PUVA or UVB phototherapy -- 4-week washout before Day 0
Investigational drugs -- 12 weeks (biologics), 5 half-lives (orals), or 2 weeks (topical)
Antihistamines, if prescribed for pruritus associated with psoriasis -- 2-week washout before Day 0
permitted_concomitant: Eye drop, ear, and nasal corticosteroid preparations are allowed
Inhaled corticosteroid preparations are allowed if used for a stable condition at a stable dose for >28 days before screening and continued at the same dose throughout the study
Non-medicated emollients, moisturizers, and sunscreens as normally used, applied to non-treated areas as needed, not within 12 hours of a study visit (none applied to treated areas)
Chronically used medications (particularly statins and anti-hypertensives) are allowed unless separately prohibited in Table 1
value.population_note: Monotherapy design (ARQ-154/roflumilast foam 0.3% QD vs vehicle foam QD to scalp and body psoriasis for the full 8-week treatment period), governed by a formal prohibited/permitted concomitant medication table (Table 1) rather than a standardized background regimen -- no background TCS or co-administered active agent.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: 4.5.1 Prohibitions and Concomitant Therapy: Prohibited medications and products are detailed in Table 1... Notes: (1) Eye drop, ear, and nasal corticosteroid preparations are allowed. Inhaled corticosteroid preparations are allowed if used for a stable condition and at a stable dose for > 28 days before screening, and are continued at the same dose throughout the study. (2) Non-medicated emollients, moisturizers and sunscreens will be allowed as used normally by the subjects. These can be applied to non-treated areas as needed and should not be used within 12 hours of a study visit. (3) No emollients or moisturizers should be applied on treated areas.

alpha_split.method: PSSI-75 gatekeeper, then Holm on PSSI-50 time-to-success, PSD change-from-baseline Week 8, PSD change-from-baseline Week 4, and PSSI-90 at Week 8
hierarchical, Week 8 then Week 4 then Week 2

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: To control for multiple comparisons among the secondary endpoints, the following testing plan will be used: Upon demonstration of statistical significance for S-IGA Success at Week 8, the secondary endpoint of B-IGA Success at Week 8 will be tested hierarchically at the 5% significance level. If the test for B-IGA Success at Week 8 is significant, the alpha of 0.05 will be split to test 2 families of secondary endpoints. The first family will be comprised of the PSSI-75, which will be tested at alpha = 0.03 level. If the test of PSSI-75 is statistically significant, the alpha=0.03 will be used with a Holm testing procedure to test the 4-endpoints of time to success in PSSI-50, CFB in Total PSD score at Week 8, CFB in Total PSD score at Week 4, and PSSI-90 at Week 8. The remaining alpha = 0.02 will be used to test the second family, comprised of the Scalp WI-NRS at Week 8, the Scalp WI-NRS at Week 4, and the Scalp WI-NRS at Week 2. The tests within this second family will be hierarchical, beginning with the endpoint at Week 8, followed by Week 4 and Week 2.

study_schedule.source_excerpt: 4.3 Subject Participation: There will be a minimum of 6 clinic visits, including Screening, Baseline, Week 2, Week 4, and Week 8, of treatment, as well as a Week 9 follow-up visit (1 week after last dose). Since the interval between the Screening and Baseline visits may be up to 4 weeks, the anticipated maximum duration of subject participation is approximately 13 weeks.
